$description: #237-T derived sort of R1's 30 tensions. Buckets are DERIVED by the rules printed in _derive_sort.py, not hand-sorted. FLOATED: nothing here is ruled.

rules.R-OBLIGATION: at least one party id has principle-register grade 'L' (OBLIGATION, s237-D1); precedence first (s237-D2)
rules.R-RESOLVED: how_it_resolves cites an s<N>-D<N> id present in knowledge/_rulings.json

rows.mediating_variable: LAYER: convention governs MECHANISM (where things are, how they behave), distinctiveness governs SIGNAL (which single element carries the moment). Also brand mandate.
rows.the_pull: Familiarity says converge on convention; distinctiveness says one element must break the pattern to be noticed or owned.
rows.how_it_resolves: Never trade them at the same layer. Diverge on signal, converge on mechanism. A brand that diverges on mechanism pays in error rate.
rows.apollo_touch: s151-D1 two-red law: one signal colour, background-keyed. The law IS a Von Restorff budget with a legal contrast floor attached.

rows.mediating_variable: WHO ABSORBS IT: user expertise and task frequency. Also whether the removed complexity is REGULATED (then it cannot be relocated off-screen at all).
rows.the_pull: Removing options from a screen does not remove them from the task; it relocates them into a later step, a setting, or a support call.
rows.how_it_resolves: Ask where the complexity went and price it there. A progressive-disclosure win that adds two steps for daily users is a loss.
rows.apollo_touch: s217-D5 bento option matrix: three types with ruled option sets is exactly this trade, made once at the system level.

rows.mediating_variable: TASK CRITICALITY and whether the user believes work is being done on their behalf. Search and underwriting benefit from visible work; a toggle does not.
rows.the_pull: One says make it instant; the other found that removing the visible work can LOWER perceived value and trust.
rows.how_it_resolves: Instant for direct manipulation; show the work for delegated tasks where the user is buying judgement, not speed.
rows.apollo_touch: Chart hover latency and skeleton states — the honest split is interaction (instant) vs computation (show the work).

rows.mediating_variable: WHO IS MEASURING: in evaluation, aesthetics is a confound to control; in shipping, it is a benefit to bank.
rows.the_pull: A beautiful surface measurably masks real defects, so the effect works AGAINST discovering them.
rows.how_it_resolves: Never let a beauty pass substitute for a task-success measurement. Yablonski's own caveat and Tuch 2012 both point this way.
rows.apollo_touch: Apollo's review pages are gorgeous and ruled by eye. That is precisely the condition under which this effect bites hardest.

rows.mediating_variable: LAYER AGAIN: tolerant at the INPUT SURFACE (normalise the phone number), strict at the BOUNDARY (validate before persisting or transmitting).
rows.the_pull: Tolerant input is kind to users and dangerous to systems; RFC 9413 argues tolerance also entrenches bugs permanently.
rows.how_it_resolves: Accept-and-normalise, then validate strictly and SHOW the normalisation. Never silently accept ambiguity.
rows.apollo_touch: Form snippets in the factory: normalising is a behaviour, and #235's behaviour address is where such a rule would live.

rows.mediating_variable: MEASUREMENT WINDOW: remembered satisfaction (peak-end wins) vs in-task completion and error rate (consistency wins).
rows.the_pull: Peak-end says spend disproportionately on one moment and the finish; consistency says an uneven journey erodes trust in the middle.
rows.how_it_resolves: Use peak-end to allocate the LAST 10% of polish, never the first 90%. A delightful confirmation on a broken journey is a measured lie.

rows.mediating_variable: DEVICE and POINTER TYPE, plus whether the target is a CONTROL (44/48) or a DATA MARK (24).
rows.the_pull: Every pixel spent enlarging a control is a pixel not spent on data, and dense dashboards are what finance actually wants.
rows.how_it_resolves: Split the rule by object class, which Apollo already did: s116-D1 exempts data marks from the 44 control floor while keeping them in the check.
rows.apollo_touch: s116-D1, s114-D3/D5 hit-area sweep. This tension is already ruled in Apollo and the ruling is more sophisticated than the law.

rows.mediating_variable: INTERRUPTION COST vs INFORMATION VALUE: how reversible is the thing the user is doing, and how time-critical is the news.
rows.the_pull: Notifications and status updates are the main destroyer of the state they are meant to support.
rows.how_it_resolves: Route by criticality: block only for irreversible or time-critical events; everything else accretes in a place the user chooses to look.
rows.apollo_touch: s135-D1 contextual notification shell — the shell exists; the ROUTING RULE does not.

rows.mediating_variable: WHOSE INTEREST: goal-gradient helps a user finish a task they chose; the artificial-progress variant serves the business.
rows.the_pull: Both are used to justify progress meters, but they predict different things: one predicts effort, the other predicts memory of the incomplete.
rows.how_it_resolves: Use real progress toward the user's own goal. Illusory progress (Kivetz's endowed head start) is the ethical line and sits near DSA Article 25.

rows.mediating_variable: TIMING: guidance attached to the moment of need beats guidance attached to first launch. Also frequency of use.
rows.the_pull: If people skip the manual, they skip the tour; but shipping no guidance leaves discoverability to chance.
rows.how_it_resolves: Replace tours with in-place signifiers and recoverable exploration. This is Tognazzini's explorable-interfaces principle doing the work.

rows.mediating_variable: REGULATORY CONTEXT and consequence asymmetry. In a bank, a rare case can be the expensive one.
rows.the_pull: The 20% that carries most volume is not the 20% that carries most regulatory risk.
rows.how_it_resolves: Rank by expected cost, not by frequency. Pareto ranks the wrong axis for regulated products.
rows.apollo_touch: The factory's quality rubric (s234-D2/D6) should carry consequence, not just frequency.

rows.mediating_variable: WHETHER THE REMOVED THING WAS REAL: was an option deleted, or moved out of sight?
rows.the_pull: Simplicity pressure meets a floor; below it, apparent simplicity is complexity that has been hidden rather than removed.
rows.how_it_resolves: Require a destination for every removed element. 'Simplified' with no named destination is a defect report waiting to be filed.

rows.mediating_variable: PREFERENCE CLARITY and EXPERTISE — the moderators Scheibehenne et al. identified. Novices with unclear preferences benefit from curation; experts do not.
rows.the_pull: Curating options for the user's benefit is one step from removing the option they needed; and the overload effect itself does not survive meta-analysis.
rows.how_it_resolves: Default to a curated set with a full set one action away. Do not cite choice overload as settled science while doing it.

rows.mediating_variable: NEITHER APPLIES: both are recall-capacity claims and a visible menu is a recognition task.
rows.the_pull: Two incompatible numbers used to justify the same layout decisions.
rows.how_it_resolves: Cite chunking (the mechanism) for grouping decisions and cite neither number for item counts. Use scanning cost instead.
rows.apollo_touch: Bento module counts (s217-D2/D5) should be justified by grouping and scanning, NOT by 7±2. The brief already flags this.

rows.mediating_variable: LEGAL: the accessibility floor is not tradeable. Brand yields, or the usage changes (size, weight, background).
rows.the_pull: Brand colours frequently fail contrast at the sizes brands want to use them.
rows.how_it_resolves: Background-keyed colour rules, which is exactly what s151-D1 does: the same semantic red resolves to a different hex per ground.
rows.apollo_touch: s151-D1, s149-D1 (mono error ink camp), s194-D1 (contrast duty attaches to label and glyph, not chrome).

rows.mediating_variable: OBJECT CLASS and the AA/AAA boundary. Controls take the enhanced floor; marks take the 24 px dense-case minimum.
rows.the_pull: AAA target size is incompatible with the density a trading or ledger view needs.
rows.how_it_resolves: Apollo's answer: adopt 2.5.5 for controls (s234-D3) and exempt marks explicitly with a named check (s116-D1). Declared exemption, not silent.
rows.apollo_touch: s234-D3 adopted 2.5.5; s116-D1 fenced data marks. The exemption is the interesting artefact.

rows.mediating_variable: SCOPE OF THE CONSTANT: grammar constant, values variable. Consistency applies to the RULE, not the hex.
rows.the_pull: Consistency argues for one look; the product requirement is four, differing per client.
rows.how_it_resolves: Exactly Apollo's per-theme derivation: one grammar, four resolutions. s202-D1 inherits console's tuned dimensions across the square themes.
rows.apollo_touch: s217-D2 (gutter is the only divergence), s202-D1 (one grammar across four themes).

rows.mediating_variable: FREQUENCY OF USE per element, and whether recall would be from the same screen or from elsewhere.
rows.the_pull: Nielsen's own heuristics 6 and 8 pull against each other on the same screen.
rows.how_it_resolves: Show what is needed for the current step; make the rest reachable without recall (search, a visible menu). The heuristics do not resolve this themselves.
rows.apollo_touch: The best in-set example of why the evaluator effect exists: two evaluators can cite opposite heuristics for opposite verdicts.

rows.mediating_variable: TRUTH and REVERSIBILITY: a real count shown honestly is persuasion; a fabricated or non-reversible one is prohibited design.
rows.the_pull: The persuasion literature is a toolkit for exactly the behaviours Article 25 prohibits.
rows.how_it_resolves: Every persuasion node in the brain needs a paired legal node. Never let a B-grade effect be retrieved without its L-grade fence.
rows.apollo_touch: A concrete argument for the graph carrying grade L at all — the brain must know 'wise' from 'mandatory'.

rows.mediating_variable: REGULATORY CONTEXT plus DECISION MOMENT. Disclosure must be present AT the decision, not one click away in a PDF.
rows.the_pull: Regulation requires that customers be equipped to decide; minimalism removes exactly the material that equips them.
rows.how_it_resolves: Layer disclosure by decision moment rather than hiding it. Test comprehension, not preference — which is what the Duty actually demands.
rows.apollo_touch: The single most under-served principle in Apollo for a bank client.

rows.mediating_variable: AUDIENCE PURPOSE: decision-support (accuracy wins) vs communication to a general audience (engagement can win, with the accuracy loss declared).
rows.the_pull: The most accurate encodings are the plainest ones.
rows.how_it_resolves: Rank encodings by accuracy first; if brand overrides, record that the override cost accuracy so it is a decision, not an accident.
rows.apollo_touch: The charts pillar and the dataviz series work — series-3 4.61:1 and the hover token set.

rows.mediating_variable: STRENGTH ORDER: common region beats proximity when they conflict. So a keyline in the wrong place silently redefines the group.
rows.the_pull: A boundary can override proximity, so keylines and spacing can assert two different groupings on the same layout.
rows.how_it_resolves: Never let spacing and keylines disagree. Apollo ruled the keyline HUGS the module rather than sitting centred in the gutter, which resolves this precisely.
rows.apollo_touch: s217-D8 keylines hug modules — the clearest Gestalt ruling in the repo, made by eye before the principle was named.

rows.mediating_variable: ACTION CONSEQUENCE: acknowledgement is always immediate; CELEBRATION is proportional.
rows.the_pull: Proportionality says do not toast every click; the response limit says acknowledge everything immediately.
rows.how_it_resolves: Separate acknowledgement (instant, quiet, always) from confirmation (proportional, sometimes loud). Most systems conflate them.

rows.mediating_variable: COST OF THE SECOND ROUTE: does it change the mental model, or just the entry point?
rows.the_pull: Offering multiple routes to a task multiplies the surface that must stay consistent.
rows.how_it_resolves: Multiple entries, one model. Two entries that behave differently are worse than one.

rows.mediating_variable: CONSENT vs CONVENIENCE and REVERSIBILITY. A default on a data-protection choice is unlawful; a default on units or theme is a kindness.
rows.the_pull: A default is a preselection; the difference is consent, not mechanics.
rows.how_it_resolves: Defaults are legal for preferences, prohibited for consent and for anything that costs the user money. Grade the SLOT, not the mechanism.
rows.apollo_touch: A generator that mints defaults needs this distinction encoded, or it will pre-tick a marketing consent by symmetry with a theme toggle.

rows.mediating_variable: LOAD TYPE: extraneous load (remove freely) vs germane/intrinsic state the task needs held (must stay visible).
rows.the_pull: Removing on-screen material to reduce load can force people to carry state in their heads instead.
rows.how_it_resolves: Before removing anything, ask what the user must now remember. Cognitive load theory's own distinction answers this and is usually skipped.

rows.mediating_variable: MECHANICAL vs INFERENTIAL: mechanical checks (contrast, target size, semantics) are reliable; judgement checks are not.
rows.the_pull: Apollo's factory goal (s234-D2) is a page 'ranked against solid UI/UX standards' — but heuristic rankings have low inter-rater reliability.
rows.how_it_resolves: Rank on mechanical criteria and report judgement criteria as flagged observations, never as a score. Dave already leans this way: 'mechanical over inference' (s234-D6).
rows.apollo_touch: s234-D2 factory goal, s234-D6 the one path-taking gate. This tension is the strongest reason the rubric must be split by check type.

rows.mediating_variable: WHETHER THE PAGE HAS STRUCTURE: the F appears when structure is absent. It is a symptom, not a target.
rows.the_pull: Designing FOR the F-pattern optimises for the failure mode; scent theory says fix the cues so scanning is not needed.
rows.how_it_resolves: Treat an F-pattern finding as a diagnostic that the page lacks scent and structure. The steward (NN/g) says the same.

rows.mediating_variable: LEGAL FLOOR plus INPUT MODALITY. Keyboard users are not a subset that can be styled away.
rows.the_pull: A conforming focus indicator is deliberately loud, and loud is what minimal designs remove first.
rows.how_it_resolves: Design the focus state as a first-class token from the start. Retrofitting it always fights the visual system.
rows.apollo_touch: Apollo adopted 2.4.13 at s234-D3 — the focus token set is where that ruling becomes real.

rows.mediating_variable: LICENCE. Some sources can be nodes; some can only be POINTERS with an access note.
rows.the_pull: The strongest empirical e-commerce evidence cannot be copied into the graph without licence breach.
rows.how_it_resolves: Carry a licence field on every source node and let the generator refuse to emit text from a no-derivatives source. Laws of UX (CC BY-NC-ND) is the same case.
rows.apollo_touch: Directly relevant to #234's generation chain: the graph must know what it may not emit.
